name: Enrique Tirabocchi
biography: Enrique Tirabocchi, also recorded as Enrico Tiraboschi, was an Italian swimmer whose sporting life was closely connected with Argentina. He lived and worked there before his Channel success, and accounts of his achievement reflect both Italian and Argentine associations. His crossing is recorded under Italy.

After unsuccessful attempts in 1921 and 1922, he completed the first recognised France-to-England swim on 12 August 1923. He landed at Shakespeare Beach, Dover, with the Calais tug Champion as his escort. The retrospective Channel record gives 16 hours and 33 minutes, substantially faster than Matthew Webb’s earlier crossing. Contemporary press histories contain competing timings, which remain qualified in the detailed record.

Tirabocchi’s success received attention on both sides of the Atlantic and made him an important figure in the growing international culture of marathon swimming. He gave his £1,000 Daily Sketch prize to the International Swimming Federation.

lines.label: Finished

lines.text: The selected finish date, 12 August 1923, and 16h33m follow the museum/CSA/TIME evidence already cited. The historical press study is internally inconsistent: its opening dates the achievement to 13 August and gives 16h23m, while its technical discussion reports 20:08 departure, 12:33 arrival and 16h25m. These are not reconciled. Structured clocks and a departure date remain unconfirmed; no date is calculated from elapsed time.
lines.label: Timing note

lines.text: CSA record 2234 supplies the name variant, Italy, route and 16:33. Dover Museum photo records d12066 and d39404 identify the 12 August completion, Shakespeare Beach landing, pilot and tug. Contemporary TIME supports the time and pioneering route. The research literature exposes remaining timing differences; no original observer record has been inspected.
